messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High GPU queue growth on prod-cluster-east-1 (svc: inference-api). Queue length increased from 120 -> 780 over 6m. Autoscaler failing to attach new GPU nodes. Priority: P1. Paging: @oncall-ryan :rotating_light:

oncall-ryan: on it. grabbing logs. any customer-facing alerts?

derek: seeing a big spike in request rate to `inference-api/v1/generate` from a single client id — looks like batch jobs. Throttles started ~12:15 UTC.

kate: Confirmed autoscaler scale-up attempts: ASG request created but instances stay in `Pending` and then fail with `InstanceLaunchError`. Cloud console shows `Launch template invalid` + `iam:PassRole` denied error on instance profile.

eng-sre-lead: stack traces / relevant logs? paste the `kube-autoscaler` event lines?

kate: from nodes events (excerpt):
``` 
0s Warning FailedCreate pod "gpu-provisioner"... failed to create instance: launch template launchTemplateId=lt-0xxxx invalid: iamInstanceProfile not found
0s Warning FailedAttachVolume ...
```

derek: also seeing taint mismatches — our GPU nodegroup expects taint `redwood.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule` but the launch template created instances with `node.kubernetes.io/uninitialized=true` (bootstrap failing).

incident-bot: Incident runbook: https://runbook.redwood.example/incidents/gpu-autoscale (invoked)

oncall-ryan: immediate mitigations: 1) scale down inference worker concurrency / reduce qps for non-critical clients 2) enable fallback to cpu-variant model for low-priority routes 3) if we can, spin up a manual GPU nodegroup with a basic launch template that uses existing known-good instance profile.

customer-success: we have two customers on dedicated SLAs seeing errors (IDs: C-982, C-174). How long until mitigation?

kate: manual ASG create attempt failed with same error — looks like the recent change to launch template `lt-inference-v3` unintentionally referenced a new instance profile `redwood-inference-gpu-profile-v2` that doesn't exist in this account/region (copy-paste mistake).

cloud-ops: confirmed: instance profile missing. The policy used by the new template requires `iam:PassRole` for `arn:aws:iam::123456:role/redwood-gpu-ec2-role`. The role exists in other regions but not eu-west-1 (this cluster region).

eng-sre-lead: root cause hypothesis: deploy of launch template changes (automated infra PR) rolled out a new LT with region-limited profile name; autoscaler uses LT to request nodes — requests fail at EC2 stage due to missing IAM resources. Because those failures are terminal, autoscaler gives up and queue grows.

oncall-ryan: immediate action plan:
- action A: revert autoscaler config to use `lt-inference-v2` (known-good) — kate to attempt rollback.
- action B: temporarily route non-SLA traffic to cpu fallback — derek/kate coordinate with API proxy.
- action C: pages to infra-owner to create missing instance profile in region (cloud-ops).

kate: rolling back autoscaler LT binding now: `kubectl -n kube-system edit cm/gpu-autoscaler-config` -> switching `launchTemplate` to `lt-inference-v2`. Applying...

ops-runbook-bot: rollback playbook step 3 executed: updated autoscaler config and triggered scale attempt. Next scale attempt in ~20s.

incident-bot: New event: autoscaler tried scaleUp at 1823478960, instances launched but showing `Instance profile not found` in EC2 response.

kate: re-applying a patched launch template that references `redwood-inference-gpu-profile` (existing) instead of the v2 name. Patch applied to `lt-inference-v3-patch`.

cloud-ops: creating instance profile in eu-west-1 with minimal policies to allow bootstrapping (KMS read, SSM, EC2 tags). ETA ~8m.

oncall-ryan: while cloud-ops does that, Derek, can you throttle the offending client? We should protect other customers.

derek: throttling rule applied at edge for client-id `acct-batch-149`. Reduced concurrency from 200 -> 20. Queue growth rate slowed immediately.

customer-success: C-982 reports 503s; C-174 intermittent latency. Notified both with incident underway and ETA 15m for mitigation.

eng-sre-lead: good. Keep me in the loop. After we get nodes up, validate `node.kubernetes.io/accelerator=nvidia-tesla-v100` label and taint present and kubelet Ready.

incident-bot: Event: cloud-ops created instance profile `redwood-inference-gpu-profile` at 1823479150.

kate: re-triggering ASG / manual launch using patched LT. Launch started.

oncall-ryan: monitoring node join events.

ops-runbook-bot: health-check script running: `kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu -o wide` every 15s.

kate: node  ip-10-0-45-234.eu-west-1.ec2.internal joined. Labels: `accelerator=nvidia-tesla-v100`, `redwood.com/gpu=true`. Taints applied: `redwood.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule`. Kubelet Ready.

derek: pods from `inference-api` started getting scheduled to the new node. backlog processing started. queue dropped from 780 -> 210 in 6m.

customer-success: C-982 reports degraded but improving, C-174 sees normal latencies. Notified customers with update.

eng-sre-lead: follow-up actions (post-incident):
- enforce CI check to verify referenced instance profiles exist in target region before LT deploys.
- add autoscaler retry/backoff telemetry to detect repeated terminal EC2 failures and surface earlier.
- add workload-level circuit breaker to fallback to cpu-model earlier if queue exceeds X for Y minutes.

oncall-ryan: preparing handoff to next oncall in 30m. docing timeline and actions in #incidents-postmortems. Also setting incident severity to P1 -> P2 after mitigation.

incident-bot: oncall-handoff scheduled to @oncall-ayana at 1823480700. Reminder will be sent 10m before.

eng-sre-lead: tagging this for postmortem. Please capture the infra PR that introduced the new LT name (PR #4521) and the deploy window.

derek: quick note: we should throttle large batch clients by default during business hours. I'll open a ticket.

oncall-ryan: final status: nodes healthy, queue processing, autoscaler config reverted and patched LT applied, customers notified. Handoff in 25m.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED -> MONITORING] Incident state changed at 1823479333.
